query: What customer issues create the most support burden?

per_column.name: customer_urgency_signal
per_column.rationale: Urgency/severity is a meaningful axis for support burden, but the values largely mirror the existing 'priority' column (p0-p3 scheme), making it substantially redundant. Values are reasonable readings of the text (immediate outage = p0, enhancement = not_urgent), though the p0/p1 labeling is an imposed severity mapping not literally in the text.

per_column.name: system_criticality
per_column.rationale: A useful topical/criticality axis to group burden by. Mostly grounded, but conflates criticality with topic (e.g. 'payment', 'feature_request'), and misfires on CS-0005: a BOM export request with a manual workaround is labeled 'production_outage', which the text does not support.

per_column.name: user_impact_scale
per_column.rationale: Blast-radius is a strong, genuinely new axis for weighing support burden. Well grounded where text is explicit (entire_tenant for the 502 affecting all Acme members; single_user for one invoice). However CS-0002 session-drop with no stated scope is confidently labeled single_user, and CS-0005 is 'small_team' though the text says only 'they', suggesting some unwarranted specifics on silent rows.

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: A sound categorical grouping axis, but it overlaps heavily with system_criticality (both carry feature_request, performance, billing/payment), reducing marginal leverage. Categorisations are mostly defensible readings, though calling the outage a generic 'bug_defect' is coarse.

per_column.name: blocking_or_workaround_status
per_column.rationale: Strong, distinct axis directly relevant to burden: whether users are blocked or have a workaround. Well grounded — CS-0005 explicitly mentions a manual sed workaround (degraded_workaround_exists), CS-0004 is an enhancement. CS-0001 'fully_blocking' is slightly debatable (invoice correction) but reasonable given the Friday deadline.

per_column.name: escalation_requirement
per_column.rationale: Which team/escalation path is needed is highly relevant to burden and offers a new operational axis. But values are frequently inferred beyond the text: CS-0005 'platform_engineering' and CS-0003 'p1_bridge_required' are plausible, yet the specific routing (legal_compliance, database_recovery) implies determinations the source text often does not explicitly state.

per_column.name: remediation_type
per_column.rationale: Type of fix is a useful axis for effort/burden. However groundedness suffers from over-confident specifics: CS-0005, an account-level toggle request with a workaround, is labeled 'configuration_change' fine, but the dominant 'urgent_hotfix_rollback' (135 rows) suggests aggressive labeling, and CS-0001 'refund_credit_reversal' when the customer only wants a corrected invoice (not a refund) is a slight overreach.

judge.rationale: The added columns collectively give several genuinely useful axes for analysing support burden — blast radius (user_impact_scale), blocking/workaround status, escalation path, and remediation type are the strongest and most distinct. Weakening the set: customer_urgency_signal largely duplicates the original 'priority' column, and issue_category overlaps considerably with system_criticality, so a few columns add limited marginal leverage. Groundedness is generally acceptable — silent-row inferences are mostly warranted — but there are observable over-reaches: the BOM/export ticket labeled 'production_outage', the invoice-correction ticket labeled 'refund_credit_reversal', and confident impact/escalation specifics on rows where the text is silent. These are imposed inferences rather than sound readings, pulling groundedness down modestly.
